name: baseline policy decisions
description: ADR-008 requires every policy to have unit tests with example inputs and expected decisions. These are those tests, expressed as data so the engine and any future re-implementation are held to the same bar. Each case asserts the effect AND the basis — an allow that matched nothing is a different outcome from an allow a rule granted, and ADR-014 exists because the two were previously indistinguishable.

rules.description: Content fetched from the open web must not drive a browser or a device.
A tool that cannot be safely replayed needs a human before it runs.
Anything estimated over five dollars is gated.
Read-only research capabilities are permitted outright.

cases.name: untrusted web content cannot reach an agent capability
the same capability without untrusted input is not denied by that rule
a non-idempotent tool needs approval at dispatch
unstated idempotency is treated as non-idempotent
cases.description: ADR-016 requires an explicit declaration; the safe reading of silence is the one that cannot replay a side effect.

cases.name: the same non-idempotent tool is not gated at plan validation by a dispatch-scoped rule
cost gate fires above the threshold
cost gate does not fire below the threshold
an untrusted tag alone does not deny a research read
cases.description: The deny rule is scoped to agent.* capabilities; a research read carrying untrusted input is still allowed, by the research rule rather than by default.

cases.name: an ungoverned action is allowed but recorded as unmatched
cases.description: This is the case ADR-014 is about. The effect is indistinguishable from a permitted action; the basis is not, and the unmatched fraction is built from exactly this.

cases.name: lower priority number wins when two rules match
cases.description: approve.expensive (priority 20) and allow.research_reads (priority 30) both match; the gate wins.

cases.name: deny wins a priority tie against allow (fail-safe)
cases.description: Two rules match at priority 0, one deny and one allow. A misordered or equally-ranked policy must fail closed, not open — this is the ordering guarantee the engine promises, and without a case for it the tie-break could be inverted and every other test would still pass.
